newsitem.title: FRANCE: French far-right mayors get mixed reviews in poll.
newsitem.headline: French far-right mayors get mixed reviews in poll.

text.p: French far-right mayors score high on security but low on culture, and are seen as badly harming the image of their towns, according to an opinion poll published on Monday.
The CSA poll was carried out 20 months after the far-right National Front won control of its first three towns, prompting constant controversy. The Front won a fourth town, Vitrolles, last month.
The survey in the daily Le Parisien said that an average 46 percent of voters in the three towns were satisfied with their mayor, against 35 percent who were not.
But in two of the towns, Toulon and Orange, a majority of voters would chose another mayor if elections were held again now. The mayor would be narrowly re-elected in the third, Marignane.

An average 40 percent of voters in all three towns said security was improving, against 20 percent who saw it deteriorating, and 46 percent said the environment was being better protected against 20 percent who said it was not.

A average 57 percent said their mayor had hurt their town's image, compared to 17 percent who disagreed. Thirty-six percent said cultural facilities were deteriorating and 27 percent said they were not.
The Front's cultural policy has led to bitter disputes.

The mayor of Orange, Jacques Bompard, has been acused of censoring municipal libraries. Toulon Mayor Jean-Marie Le Chevallier came into open conflict with the Culture Ministry and intellectuals for cancelling a tribute to a Jewish writer and sacking the head of the local ballet theatre.
